title: Super Session: Future-Proofing Your Design Career in the Age of AI
note: Placeholder transcript for the AI Week demo, not a real transcription. Replace via generate_transcripts.py once ffmpeg + an OpenAI/Whisper key are available.

segments.text: Panel frames AI as a collaborator that removes production grunt work, not a replacement for creative judgment, and sets up the rest of the session around that distinction.
Discussion of uniquely human skills that stay valuable regardless of tooling: taste, storytelling, empathy for a user or audience, and knowing which idea is worth pursuing.
Reskilling and portfolio strategy - what to add to a portfolio now (process, rationale, iteration) versus polished final shots alone, since AI makes final shots cheap to produce.
Side-by-side case studies comparing fully AI-generated work against AI-assisted work where a human directed every key decision, and why clients still pay differently for each.
Ethical considerations: attribution, training-data provenance, and how the panelists vet which AI tools they'll actually use on client work.
Staying adaptable: treating new AI features as just another material to learn, the same way past generations learned new software, rather than a threat to specialize away from.
The value of community and mentorship during this shift - pairing junior designers with seniors specifically to transfer judgment, not just tool proficiency.
Closing call to action: pick one workflow this month to augment with AI, keep the creative decisions your own, and measure whether it actually gave time back for better work.
